Bug_Details:
Calling toString on an array does not provide useful information The toString method on an array will print its identity, such as
[I@4488aabb. This is almost never needed. Use Arrays.toString to print a
human-readable summary.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is demonstrated by calling the toString method on an array, which results in printing the array's identity hash code instead of its contents. This is not useful for debugging or logging purposes.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method with an integer array. The method returns the result of calling toString on the array, which is then asserted against the expected human-readable string. This assertion fails because the toString method returns the object's identity hash code instead.
